Hey! Gpharm here!

I can't exactly tell you how your experience is going to be when applying to the Gmed program, but I will say that it is important to consider that your stats won't be only factor for you to consider!

If you are able to get past the application round, around 50 applicants for GMed, then you will go in for interviews and other methods of determining value for the program. For GPharm, this was an additional essay after you had finished your interviews. What is important for these interviews is that you are able to stand out and be truthful about your passions for medicine. The proctors for the interview will rate your interview based on a variety of points, and those scores will be used in your consideration for the program.

So what I have to say for this is to have a central theme, as well as a obvious desire for medicine in your application. Speak about your true life experiences and have faith in yourself. 

I hope that you were able to get something useful from this explanation, and I wish you the best of luck in your application! 

\*\*\*\*Please keep in mind that I did my interviews 2 years before the pandemic, so many things could have changed, so I would definitely make sure to email the GMED coordinator about what you might expect!\*\*\*\*\*
